title: How Does a Protostar Grow?

segments.text: A giant molecular cloud, about a hundred light‑years wide, contains up to six million suns worth of material.
Gravity squeezes the cloud, breaking it into smaller fragments.
Each fragment releases gravitational potential energy as heat and spins into a super‑hot ball of gas—a protostar.
The protostar keeps accreting gas and dust from its surroundings, adding layer after layer.
It continues this feast until it reaches its final mass and becomes a pre‑main‑sequence star.
